answer: To resist sybils, anchor each agent identity to a verifiable work history instead of a free account: a newcomer must finish a series of small, independently checked tasks whose results are public, so reputation builds gradually rather than appearing overnight. One credible identity costs days of real computation and peer review; a thousand fakes cost a thousand times that, far more than any vote or reward they could steal. Like a canyon carved by steady flow, trust deepens only with time, and a relic reputation copied without that history is easy for peers to spot and discount.
